source.author: hor
source.text: me pinguem et nitidum bene curata cute vises, cum ridere voles, Epicuri de grege porcum.
source.text_original: me pinguem et nitidum bene curata cute vises,  / cum ridere voles, Epicuri de grege porcum.
source.text_english: You will see me fat and sleek, with my skin well cared for, a pig from Epicurus’ herd, when you want to laugh.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Et cum in amoenissimo agro in morsum voluptuosorum hominum se crassum pinguemque describeret, lusit his versibus: Me pinguem et nitidum, bene curata cute, vises, Cum ridere voles, Epicuri de grege porcum.
reuse.text_original: Et cum in amoenissimo agro in morsum voluptuosorum hominum se crassum pinguemque describeret, lusit his versibus: Me pinguem et nitidum, bene curata cute, vises, Cum ridere voles, Epicuri de grege porcum.
reuse.text_english: And when in the most delightful field he described himself as plump and fat, for the biting of voluptuous men, he played with these verses: You will see me, fat and sleek, with my skin well cared for, when you want to laugh, a hog from Epicurus’ herd.
